Loko nhulu yi va slimy kumbe yi nun'hwa ammonia swinene, engetela dry browns kutani u yi hundzuluxa.

Kambela ku tsakama na moya loko nhulu yi ri karhi yi cinca; ndlela yin'we yo hlanganisa a yi ringani eka nkatsakanyo wun'wana ni wun'wana wa swilo leswi tirhisiweke.

Xiphemu xa le xikarhini xa nhulu lexi hisaka a xi tiyisisi leswaku xiphemu xin’wana ni xin’wana xa nhulu xi treated. Nkarhi, temperature ni ndlela yo yi lawula hinkwato swi na nkoka.

Hlayisani nyama, dairy, swimilani leswi vabyaka, pet waste na contaminated materials swi ri ehandle ka ndlela leyi olovaka ya ndyangu.

U nga teki leswaku home composting yi lovisa weed seed yin'wana ni yin'wana kumbe disease organism yin'wana ni yin'wana. Tirhisa recognised process laha sanitation yi lavekaka.

Hlayisani wattle seed pods ehandle ka nhulu ya compost. Nhulu leyi tolovelekeke yi nga ha ka yi nga endli mbewu yin’wana ni yin’wana yi va non-viable.

Tirhisa swilo leswi baseke, leswi untreated ntsena. Bark yi bola hi ku nonoka; vito ra yona ntsena a hi vumbhoni bya leswaku a yi na contamination.

Kambela nhulu kutani u yi hundzuluxa loko yi lava moya wo tala kumbe ku hlanganisiwa. Yi hlayise yi tsakamile, ku nga ri waterlogged.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Balance browns, greens, moisture and air
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Ringanisa browns, greens, ku tsakama ni moya.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A hot centre does not prove the whole heap is sanitised
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Xiphemu xa le xikarhini lexi hisaka a xi tiyisisi leswaku nhulu hinkwayo yi sanitised.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep seed pods and contaminated materials out
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa seed pods na contaminated materials swi ri handle ka nhulu.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Judge readiness from the compost condition, not a fixed regional timetable
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Kambela ku lungheka ka compost hi xiyimo xa yona, ku nga ri hi regional timetable leyi vekiweke.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer's compost heap smells strongly of ammonia and is wet and slimy. What's the fix?
question.xitsongaDraft: Nhulu ya compost ya murimi yi nun'hwa ammonia swinene naswona yi tsakama yi tlhela yi va slimy. Ku lulamisa i yini?

options.sourceEnglish: Add more nitrogen-rich green material
options.xitsongaDraft: Engetela green material yo tala leyi fuweke hi nitrogen

options.sourceEnglish: Add more dry carbon material like straw and turn the heap
options.xitsongaDraft: Engetela carbon material yo oma yo tala, yo fana na straw, kutani u hundzuluxa nhulu.

options.sourceEnglish: Stop turning it and let it cool
options.xitsongaDraft: Tshika ku hundzuluxa nhulu kutani u yi tshika yi hola

options.sourceEnglish: Add more water — the smell means it's too dry
options.xitsongaDraft: Engetela mati yo tala — nun'hwelo wu vula leswaku yi omile ngopfu

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet, slimy heap may need more air and drier material. Add dry browns and turn the heap to open it up. An ammonia smell can also suggest too much nitrogen-rich material. Check that the heap stays damp, not soggy.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Nhulu leyi tsakamaka, yi slimy yi nga lava moya wo tala na swilo swo oma ku tlurisa leswi nga kona. Engetela dry browns kutani u hundzuluxa nhulu leswaku yi pfuleka. Nun'hwelo wa ammonia na wona wu nga komba nitrogen-rich material yo tala ngopfu. Kambela leswaku nhulu yi sala yi tsakamile, ku nga ri soggy.

question.sourceEnglish: Why keep wattle seed pods out of an ordinary compost heap?
question.xitsongaDraft: Ha yini u fanele ku hlayisa wattle seed pods handle ka nhulu ya compost leyi tolovelekeke?

options.sourceEnglish: Bark makes every heap too hot
options.xitsongaDraft: Bark yi endla leswaku nhulu yin'wana ni yin'wana yi hisa ngopfu

options.sourceEnglish: Some seeds may survive and spread when the compost is used
options.xitsongaDraft: Mbewu tin'wana ti nga ha pona kutani ti hangalaka loko compost yi tirhisiwa

options.sourceEnglish: Pods always attract termites
options.xitsongaDraft: Pods ti koka termites minkarhi hinkwayu

options.sourceEnglish: Pods release a gas that kills every soil organism
options.xitsongaDraft: Pods ti humesa gas leyi dlayaka soil organism yin'wana ni yin'wana

rationale.sourceEnglish: An ordinary heap may not expose every seed to conditions that make it non-viable. Excluding pods avoids spreading them with the compost.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Nhulu leyi tolovelekeke yi nga ha ka yi nga fikisi mbewu yin’wana ni yin’wana eka swiyimo leswi yi endlaka yi va non-viable. Ku susa pods swi papalata ku ti hangalasa na compost.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Two patches of soil under the same sun: bare ground cracked and dry, mulched ground still dark and moist.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Swiphemu swimbirhi swa misava ehansi ka dyambu rin'we: misava leyi nga funengetiwangi yi pandzekile naswona yi omile; misava leyi nga na mulch ya ha ri ya ntima naswona yi tsakamile.

title.sourceEnglish: Mulching and Cover Crops: Protecting and Building Soil
title.xitsongaDraft: Ku Tirhisa Mulch na Cover Crops: Ku Sirhelela Misava na Building Soil

body.sourceEnglish:
Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.

Mulch can reduce evaporation, soften the impact of rain and suppress weeds.

Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.

Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.

The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.

Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.

Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.

Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.

Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.

A Highveld field left bare after the maize harvest faces two main risks.

Winter wind can carry away dry topsoil.

The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.

Cover crops, mulch, and organic matter can help hold soil in place and help it stay alive.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Funengetani misava leyi nga funengetiwangiki hi mulch leyi basekile, leyi faneleke, yo fana na straw, byanyi byo oma kumbe wood chips.

Mulch yi nga hunguta evaporation; yi nga olovisa ku ba ka mpfula naswona yi nga sivela nhova.

Yi hlayiseni ekule na trunks and stems. Kambelani ku tsakama ehansi ka yona, mi lulamisa layer; mulch yo tala a yi vuli leswaku swi ta antswa nkarhi wun'wana ni wun'wana.

Cover crops ti nga sirhelela misava leyi nga kona exikari ka main crops. Ti hlawuleni hi ku ya hi maxelo ya laha, mati lama kumekaka ni ku byala loku landzelaka.

Swikombiso swa dyondzo swi katsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Kambelani loko swi fanele ndhawu ya kwalaho mi nga si swi byala.

Legumes ti lava bacteria leti faneleke ni swiyimo leswi faneleke swa ku kula leswaku ti fix nitrogen. Nutrients leti nga eka masalela ya tona ta kumeka loko material yi ri karhi yi bola.

Worm farms ti nga hundzuluxa food scraps ni bedding leswi faneleke swi va castings. Kambelani xibye ematshan'weni yo langutela siku ra ntshovelo leri vekiweke.

Liquid leyi khulukaka hi ntumbuluko yi huma eka worm bin yi vuriwa leachate. A yi fani na worm-casting tea leyi lunghisiweke.

Leachate yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances leswi nga ni khombo. U nga yi tirhisi eka edible plants. U nga ehleketi leswaku dilution yi endla leswaku yi hlayiseka.

Nsimu ya Highveld leyi tshikiweke yi nga funengetiwangi endzhaku ka ntshovelo wa maize yi langutana ni makhombo mambirhi lamakulu.

Mheho wa xixika wu nga susa misava ya le henhla leyi omeke.

Xidzedze xo sungula xo tika xa ximun’wana xi nga hlasela misava leyi nga funengetiwangi, xi onha vuandlalo ni xivumbeko xa yona. Loko mati ma khuluka ehenhla ka nsimu, ma nga teka misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma famba na yona.

Swibyariwa swo sirhelela misava (cover crops), mulch ni organic matter swi nga pfuna ku khoma misava endhawini ya yona ni ku yi pfuna leswaku yi ya mahlweni yi hanya.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil with suitable cover
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Sirhelela misava leyi paluxiweke hi swilo leswi faneleke swo yi funengeta.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep mulch away from trunks and stems
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa mulch ekule na trunks na stems.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Choose cover crops for local water, weather and the following crop
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlawula cover crops hi ku ya hi mati ya laha, maxelo ni crop leyi landzelaka.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Worm-bin leachate is not automatically safe fertiliser; keep it off edible plants
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Worm-bin leachate a yi fanelanga ku tekiwa yi ri fertiliser leyi hlayisekeke hi yoxe; yi hlayise ekule na edible plants.

question.sourceEnglish: A Highveld farmer harvests maize in April and leaves the field bare all winter. What are the two main risks?
question.xitsongaDraft: Murimi wa Highveld u tshovela maize hi April kutani a siya nsimu yi nga funengetiwangi xixika hinkwaxo. Hi wahi makhombo mambirhi lamakulu?

options.sourceEnglish: Overheating in winter sun and waterlogging from rain
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku hisa ngopfu ehansi ka dyambu ra xixika ni waterlogging leyi vangiwaka hi mpfula

options.sourceEnglish: Frost kills soil life and weeds take over early
options.xitsongaDraft: Frost yi dlaya soil life naswona nhova yi talela ndhawu ka ha ri eku sunguleni

options.sourceEnglish: Wind erosion of dry topsoil and loss of soil structure from spring storm impact
options.xitsongaDraft: Wind erosion ya topsoil leyi omeke (misava ya le henhla) ni ku lahlekeriwa hi soil structure hi ku ba ka spring storm

options.sourceEnglish: Soil pH drops and nitrogen builds up
options.xitsongaDraft: Soil pH ya hunguteka naswona nitrogen ya hlengeletana

rationale.sourceEnglish: Bare soil is exposed to winter wind, which can carry away dry topsoil. Raindrop impact can damage the surface; where water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Misava leyi nga funengetiwangi yi va erivaleni eka mheho wa xixika, lowu nga susaka topsoil leyi omeke (misava ya le henhla). Ku ba ka marhonsi ya mpfula ku nga onha vuandlalo; laha mati ma khulukaka ehenhla ka nsimu, ma nga teka misava leyi ntshunxekeke ma yi susa.

question.sourceEnglish: What should you remember about liquid draining from a worm bin?
question.xitsongaDraft: U fanele ku tsundzuka yini hi liquid leyi khulukaka yi huma eka worm bin?

options.sourceEnglish: It is always safe on salad leaves
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi hlayisekile minkarhi hinkwayu eka salad leaves

options.sourceEnglish: It can contain harmful organisms or substances; dilution is not a safety guarantee
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances leswi nga ni khombo; dilution a hi safety guarantee

options.sourceEnglish: It is identical to finished worm castings
options.xitsongaDraft: Yi fana hi ku helela na finished worm castings

options.sourceEnglish: A fixed dilution makes every liquid safe
options.xitsongaDraft: Dilution yo karhi leyi vekiweke yi endla leswaku liquid yin'wana ni yin'wana yi hlayiseka

rationale.sourceEnglish: Leachate is liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin. Its composition varies, so it must not be presented as a guaranteed safe feed for edible crops.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Leachate i liquid leyi khulukaka hi ntumbuluko yi huma eka worm bin. Composition ya yona ya hambana, hikokwalaho a yi fanelanga ku kombisiwa yi ri feed leyi tiyisekisiweke leswaku yi hlayisekile eka edible crops.

title.sourceEnglish: Water Harvesting

description.sourceEnglish: Swales, berms, dams, rainwater tanks and greywater — slow, spread and sink every drop.
description.sesothoDraft: Meralo ya mekero le marako a mobu (swales le berms), matamo, ditanka tsa metsi a pula le metsi a ditshila a malapeng (greywater) — fokotsa lebelo, phatlalatsa mme o tebise lerothodi le leng le le leng.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Concept cross-section of a level contour swale with a raised mound below it. Arrows show runoff slowing and spreading; infiltration depends on the soil and site.
infographicAlt.sesothoDraft: Setshwantsho sa concept cross-section sa level contour swale se nang le qubu e phahamisitsweng ka tlase ho yona. Metsu e bontsha ho fokotseha ha lebelo le ho hasana ha runoff; infiltration e itshetlehile ka mobu le setsha.

title.sourceEnglish: Swales and Berms: Slowing Water on the Slope
title.sesothoDraft: Mekero le Marako a Mobu (Swales le Berms): Ho Fokotsa Lebelo la Metsi Letswapong

body.sourceEnglish:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
body.sesothoDraft:
Mofuta o mong wa swale ke level trench on contour. E fokotsa lebelo mme e hasanya runoff, hore metsi a mang a kgone ho kenella mobung o loketseng. Di-swale tse ding di radilwe ka grade e nyenyane, e laolwang ho tsamaisa metsi a feteletseng butle ho ya safe outlet. Mokgwa o loketseng naha ya hao o itshetlehile ka mobu, letswapo, drainage le storm flow. Pele o tjheka, kopa moeletsi wa sebaka seo ya kwetlisitsweng hore a hlahlobe mola, overflow le receiving point.

Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm ka lehlakoreng le theohelang, moo difate di ka jalwang teng ha moralo wa setsha o loketse.

Difate tse jalwang moo di ka sebedisa metsi a bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka setsha.

Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rala tsela e bolokehileng ya overflow pele o tjheka.

Tsela ha e a lokela ho baka kgoholeho moepeng kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa letamo di tlameha ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.

Kopa moeletsi wa sebaka seo ya kwetlisitsweng hore a hlahlobe mobu, letswapo le storm flow. Setshwantsho hase moralo wa kaho.

Letswapo feela ha le bolele hore swale e loketse. Mobu, drainage, mobu o sa tsitsang le metsi a tswang hodimo ho letswapo kaofela di bohlokwa.

Boloka sekwahelo se setle sa mobu. Fumana tlhahlobo ya sebaka seo pele o tjheka sebakeng se moepa, se metsi kapa se sa tsitsang. Dithibelo tsa jwang le terraces le tsona di hloka moralo o loketseng setsha.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A level contour swale can hold runoff for infiltration on a suitable site; other swales need a designed grade and safe outlet
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Level contour swale e ka tshwara runoff bakeng sa infiltration setsheng se loketseng; di-swale tse ding di hloka grade e radilweng le safe outlet

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep good ground cover and plan a safe overflow
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Boloka sekwahelo se setle sa mobu mme o rale tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a mangata a tswelang kantle

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Assess soil, drainage, slope and storm flow before digging
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Lekola mobu, tsamaiso ya metsi (drainage), letswapo le phallo ya sefefo pele o tjheka

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A concept picture is not a construction design
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Setshwantsho sa mohopolo hase moralo wa kaho

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer planned a level contour swale. After heavy rain, one end holds most of the water. What should the farmer check before changing the earthwork?
question.sesothoDraft: Sehwai se rerile level contour swale. Ka mora pula e matla, ntlha e nngwe e tshwere boholo ba metsi. Sehwai se lokela ho hlahloba eng pele se fetola earthwork?

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the trench can be made deeper without a site check
options.sesothoDraft: Hore na mokero o ka etswa o tebileng haholwanyane ntle le tlhahlobo ya setsha

options.sourceEnglish: The intended design and measured levels with a trained local adviser; an unintended low point may be present
options.sesothoDraft: Moralo o neng o rerilwe le maemo a lekotsweng le moeletsi ya rutilweng wa sebaka seo; ho ka ba le sebaka se tlase se neng se sa rerwa

options.sourceEnglish: Whether a new dam at the lowest point will catch every overflow
options.sesothoDraft: Hore na letamo le letjha sebakeng se tlase ka ho fetisisa le tla tshwara phallo e nngwe le e nngwe ya metsi a tletseng

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the soil should be compacted to stop all infiltration
options.sesothoDraft: Hore na mobu o lokela ho pitlwa ho emisa ho teba hohle ha metsi

rationale.sourceEnglish: A level contour design should spread water along its length. Uneven filling may indicate an unintended low point, but some swales are intentionally graded to a safe outlet. Check the actual design, soil and overflow route before altering it.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Moralo wa level contour o lokela ho hasanya metsi boleleleng ba wona. Uneven filling ho ka bontsha sebaka se tlase se neng se sa rerwa, empa di-swale tse ding di etswa ka boomo ka grade e lebisang ho safe outlet. Hlahloba moralo wa sebele, mobu le tsela ya overflow pele o e fetola.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to control erosion on steep land. What should she do before digging?
question.sesothoDraft: Sehwai se batlang ho laola kgoholeho mobung o moepa se lokela ho etsa eng pele se tjheka?

options.sourceEnglish: Standard swales dug as deep as possible
options.sesothoDraft: Mekero (swales) e tlwaelehileng e tjhekilweng ka botebo bo phahameng ka hohle kamoo ho ka kgonehang

options.sourceEnglish: Keep ground covered and get a site assessment for suitable erosion controls
options.sesothoDraft: Ho boloka mobu o kwahetswe le ho fumana tlhahlobo ya setsha bakeng sa taolo e loketseng ya kgoholeho

options.sourceEnglish: A large dam at the bottom to catch all runoff
options.sesothoDraft: Letamo le leholo tlase ho tshwara metsi ohle a phallang

options.sourceEnglish: Compacting the soil surface with a roller
options.sesothoDraft: Ho pitla bokahodimo ba mobu ka rolara

rationale.sourceEnglish: Slope alone is not enough to choose an earthwork. Soil, drainage, stability and storm flow must also be assessed.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Letswapo feela ha le a lekana ho kgetha mosebetsi wa mobu. Mobu, tsamaiso ya metsi (drainage), botsitso le phallo ya sefefo le tsona di tlameha ho lekolwa.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: A farm dam cut through the middle: water flowing in at one end, the stored body of water, a spillway at the top edge for overflow, and a planted bank holding the soil.
infographicAlt.sesothoDraft: Letamo la polasi le sehilweng hara: metsi a kenang ntlheng e nngwe, bongata ba metsi a bolokilweng, tsela ya metsi a tletseng (spillway) ntlheng e kahodimo bakeng sa phallo e tletseng, le lebopo le jetsweng le tshwereng mobu.

title.sourceEnglish: Farm Dams and Ponds: Storing Water for the Dry Season
title.sesothoDraft: Matamo a Polasi le Matangwana: Ho Boloka Metsi Bakeng sa Sehla sa Komelelo

body.sourceEnglish:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
body.sesothoDraft:
Letamo kapa letangwana le ka boloka metsi a phallang, empa bongata bo fumanehang bo itshetlehile ka pula ya sebaka seo, sebaka se kgoboketsang metsi (catchment), tahlehelo le hore na o sebedisa metsi a makae.

Dihla tsa pula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa (South Africa). Sebedisa ditlaleho tsa sebaka seo mme o rale bakeng sa dry periods; letamo le tletseng ha le a tiisetswa.

Pele o fetola tsela ya noka kapa molatswana (watercourse) kapa o haha meaho ya polokelo, hlahloba tumello e hlokahalang le balaodi ba metsi.

Letamo le hloka dipatlisiso tsa setsha le moralo o entsweng ke motho ya nang le ditshwaneleho tse loketseng. Metsi a phallang ho tswa sebakeng sa pokellelo (catchment runoff), mobu, metheo, kotsi e ka tlase (downstream risk) le tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a tletseng (safe spillway) kaofela a bohlokwa.

O se ke wa nka hore pula ya selemo le selemo e o jwetsa boholo ba morwallo kapa polokelo eo o tla ba le yona.

Phallo e sa laolweng ya metsi a tletseng e ka kgohola le ho pshatla lerako. Rala tsela e bolokehileng bakeng sa metsi a feteletseng pele ho kaho.

Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation le seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

Boloka spillway e sa thibehang mme o hlokomele sekwahelo sa lebopo se boletsweng moralong. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.

Diphoofolo di ka senya mabopo mme tsa eketsa mantle ka hara metsi. Ho ba teng ha tsona ha ho etse hore metsi a hlweke kapa a bolokehe.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A dam needs a site assessment and qualified design
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Letamo le hloka tlhahlobo ya setsha le moralo o tswang ho motho ya nang le ditshwaneleho

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Design a safe spillway before construction
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Rala tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a tletseng (spillway) pele ho kaho

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Check required water authorisations before building
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Hlahloba ditumello tse hlokahalang tsa metsi pele o haha

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Maintain bank cover and keep trees off an earth dam wall
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Hlokomela sekwahelo sa lebopo mme o se ke wa lema difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer builds a dam wall with no spillway. After an exceptional storm it overflows. What's the likely result?
question.sesothoDraft: Sehwai se haha lerako la letamo le se nang tsela ya metsi a tletseng (spillway). Kamora sefefo se sa tlwaelehang le a kgaphatseha. Ke eng se ka bang sephetho?

options.sourceEnglish: The water irrigates lower fields beneficially
options.sesothoDraft: Metsi a nosetsa masimo a ka tlase ka mokgwa o molemo

options.sourceEnglish: It overtops and erodes the wall, risking a catastrophic breach
options.sesothoDraft: A tlola hodimo mme a kgohola lerako, a beha kotsing ya ho pshatleha ho hoholo

options.sourceEnglish: The dam stays full and overflow drains harmlessly
options.sesothoDraft: Letamo le dula le tletse mme metsi a tletseng a tswa ntle le kotsi

options.sourceEnglish: Storage capacity increases permanently
options.sesothoDraft: Bokgoni ba polokelo bo eketseha ka ho sa feleng

rationale.sourceEnglish: Without a designed overflow route, excess water finds its own way over the wall — and that uncontrolled flow is what erodes and eventually breaches it.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Ntle le tsela e radilweng ya metsi a feteletseng, metsi a feteletseng a iphumanela tsela hodima lerako — mme phallo eo e sa laolweng ke yona e kgoholang le ho qetella e pshatla lerako.

question.sourceEnglish: Which action helps protect an earth dam?
question.sesothoDraft: Ke ketso efe e thusang ho sireletsa letamo la mobu?

options.sourceEnglish: A deep, exposed dam with no bank vegetation
options.sesothoDraft: Letamo le tebileng, le pepesitsweng le se nang dimela tsa lebopo

options.sourceEnglish: Maintain the designed bank cover and keep the spillway clear
options.sesothoDraft: Ho hlokomela sekwahelo sa lebopo se radilweng le ho boloka spillway e sa thibehang

options.sourceEnglish: A full concrete lining and plastic cover
options.sesothoDraft: Ho le kwahela ka konkreite ka botlalo le sekwahelo sa polasetiki

options.sourceEnglish: A larger surface area to spread evaporation evenly
options.sesothoDraft: Sebaka se seholwanyane sa bokahodimo ho phatlalatsa mouwane ka ho lekana

rationale.sourceEnglish: A clear spillway and maintained banks help the dam work as designed. Trees should not be planted on an earth dam wall.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Spillway e sa thibehang le mabopo a hlokometsweng di thusa letamo ho sebetsa jwalo ka moralo. Difate ha di a lokela ho jalwa hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Rain running off a roof into a gutter and down a pipe into a tank, with a small first-flush diverter branching off before the tank to throw away the dirty first water.
infographicAlt.sesothoDraft: Pula e phallang hodima marulelo e kena ka hara koto ebe e theoha ka phala ho kena ka hara tanka, e nang le sekgelo se senyenyane sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se kgelohang pele ho tanka ho lahla metsi a pele a ditshila.

title.sourceEnglish: Rainwater Tanks and Roof Catchment: Collecting and Protecting Water
title.sesothoDraft: Ditanka tsa Metsi a Pula le Pokello ya Marulelo: Ho Bokella le ho Sireletsa Metsi

body.sourceEnglish:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
body.sesothoDraft:
Marulelo a hao a ka bokella metsi a pula. Bongata bo itshetlehile ka boholo ba marulelo, pula le tahlehelo.

Hlahloba hore na thepa ya marulelo e loketse ho bokella metsi a pula pele o hokela tanka.

Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Jwale o nahanele metsi a sa keneng ka gutter, a kgeloswang kapa a tsholohang tankeng e tletseng.

Palo ya pula ya selemo kaofela ha e o bolelle hore na metsi a makae a tla fumaneha nakong ya dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le ditshebediso tseo o di rerileng.

Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. First-flush diverter e thibela metsi a mang a phallo ya pele ho kena ka tankeng.

Bongata bo lokelang ho kgeloswa bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Latela ditaelo tsa mofani mabapi le ho lekanya boholo le ho hlokomela; ha ho volume e le nngwe bakeng sa marulelo ohle.

Sekgelo (diverter) ha se etse hore metsi a setseng a bolokehele ho nowa.

Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, sebaka sa marulelo le bolelele ba dry periods.

Ngola ditshebediso tse rerilweng mme o hakanye tlhoko ya tsona o sebedisa ditlaleho tsa hao. Bapisa tlhoko ya tsona le phepelo ho pholletsa le dihla.

Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a se a le manyenyane. Lebitso la provense feela ha le bolele boholo ba tanka boo o bo hlokang.

Kwahela tanka, kwahela masoba ka mesh e thibelang dikokonyana, mme o hlokomele marulelo, mekero ya marulelo (gutters) le sekgelo (diverter). Arola metsi a pula le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.

Metsi a shebahalang a hlakile a ntse a ka ba le dikokwana-hloko kapa dikhemikhale. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.

Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rain, demand and losses determine useful storage
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Boholo ba marulelo, pula, tlhoko le tahlehelo di lekanya polokelo e nang le molemo

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter for the roof
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Bontsha boholo le ho hlokomela sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) bakeng sa marulelo

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Clear water can still contain germs or chemicals
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Metsi a hlakileng a ka nna a ba le dikokwana-hloko kapa dikhemikhale

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Testing and treatment must match the intended use
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Diteko le kalafo di tlameha ho tsamaisana le tshebediso e rerilweng

question.sourceEnglish: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.sesothoDraft: Ke tlhahisoleseding efe e hlokahalang ho kgetha tanka ya metsi a pula?

options.sourceEnglish: Only the province where the farm is located
options.sesothoDraft: Feela provense moo polasi e leng teng

options.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rainfall pattern, water demand and collection losses
options.sesothoDraft: Boholo ba marulelo, mokgwa wa pula, tlhoko ya metsi le tahlehelo ya pokello

options.sourceEnglish: Only the amount of rain in one storm
options.sesothoDraft: Feela bongata ba pula sefefong se le seng

options.sourceEnglish: Only the price of the biggest available tank
options.sesothoDraft: Feela theko ya tanka e kgolo ka ho fetisisa e fumanehang

rationale.sourceEnglish: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand through wet and dry periods. One fixed regional size cannot do that.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Moralo wa tanka o tlameha ho bapisa phepelo e ka sebediswang le tlhoko ho pholletsa le dinako tsa pula le komello. Boholo bo le bong bo tsitsitseng ba sebaka bo ke ke ba etsa seo.

question.sourceEnglish: Why does a first-flush diverter matter even for irrigation-only tank water?
question.sesothoDraft: Hobaneng sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se le bohlokwa le bakeng sa metsi a tanka a sebedisetswang nosetso feela?

options.sourceEnglish: It doesn't matter for irrigation, only drinking water
options.sesothoDraft: Ha se na taba bakeng sa nosetso, feela metsing a nowang

options.sourceEnglish: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops
options.sesothoDraft: Phallo ya pele e jara mantle a teteaneng, lerole le dikokwana-hloko tse bakang mafu tse ka silafatsang dijalo tse jewang

options.sourceEnglish: It's more acidic and changes soil pH over time
options.sesothoDraft: E na le asiti e ngata mme e fetola pH ya mobu ha nako e ntse e ya

options.sourceEnglish: It stops the tank overfilling in storms
options.sesothoDraft: E thibela tanka ho tlala ho tlola meeding nakong ya difefo

rationale.sourceEnglish: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that later water is safe. Assess quality for the intended use.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Ho kgelosa metsi a pele a phallang ho ka fokotsa tshilafalo, empa ha ho tiise hore metsi a morao a bolokehile. Lekola boleng bakeng sa tshebediso e rerilweng.

title.sourceEnglish: Greywater: Check Before Reuse
title.sesothoDraft: Metsi a Ditshila a Malapeng (Greywater): Hlahloba Pele o Sebedisa Hape

body.sourceEnglish:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
body.sesothoDraft:
Metsi a sebedisitsweng ka lapeng a ka ba le dikokwana-hloko, matswai, dihlahiswa tsa ho hlwekisa le dintho tse ding. Ditaelo ha di hlalose mohlodi o mong le o mong ka tsela e tshwanang. Ditaelo tsa Afrika Borwa di fapana mabapi le metsi a khitjhineng le metsi a ho hlatswa diaparo.

O se ke wa kenya metsi a ntlwana, metsi a tswang ho nappies, a ho hlatswa motho ya kulang kapa a ho hlatswa diphoofolo moralong wa ho sebedisa metsi hape. O se ke wa sebedisa hape metsi a nang le dikhemikhale tse kotsi.

Pele ho tshebediso efe kapa efe ya metsi hape, kopa masepala le qualified local sanitation adviser hore ba hlahlobe mohlodi o tobileng, ditshebeletso tsa metsi le sanitation tsa lelapa, tshebediso e rerilweng le setsha. Haeba keletso ena e sa fumanehe kapa e sa hlaka, o se ke wa sebedisa metsi hape.

Setshwantsho se akaretsang hase moralo wa polasi. Mobu le mulch ha di disinfect wastewater. Boloka wastewater hole le drinking-water plumbing mme o thibele ho kopana ha yona le batho kapa diphoofolo. O se ke wa e fafatsa, wa e tlohela e eme, kapa wa dumella hore e phalle kantle ho property ho kena seterateng, drain kapa watercourse.

Haeba tsamaiso ya ho sebedisa metsi hape e se e sebetsa mme metsi a nkga hampe, a bokellana a eme kapa a senya dimela, emisa ho a sebedisa mme o batle keletso ho qualified local adviser.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Water sources and greywater guidance can differ
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Mehlodi ya metsi le ditaelo tsa metsi a ditshila (greywater) di ka fapana

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Check the source, service status, intended use and site locally before any reuse
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Hlahloba mohlodi, service status, tshebediso e rerilweng le setsha sebakeng seo pele ho tshebediso efe kapa efe ya metsi hape

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Mobu le mulch ha di disinfect wastewater

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Prevent contact, spray, pooling, runoff and drinking-water cross-connections
keyPoints.sesothoDraft: Thibela ho kopana le metsi, ho a fafatsa, ho a tlohela a bokellana a eme, runoff le drinking-water cross-connections

question.sourceEnglish: What should happen before any household washwater is reused?
question.sesothoDraft: Ho lokela ho etsahala eng pele metsi afe kapa afe a ho hlatswa a lapeng a sebediswa hape?

options.sourceEnglish: Direct it below mulch around a tree
options.sesothoDraft: A ise ka tlase ho mulch ho potoloha sefate

options.sourceEnglish: Ask the municipality and a qualified sanitation adviser to check the source, service status, intended use and site
options.sesothoDraft: Kopa masepala le qualified sanitation adviser hore ba hlahlobe mohlodi, service status, tshebediso e rerilweng le setsha

options.sourceEnglish: Use it if it looks clear
options.sesothoDraft: A sebedise haeba a shebahala a hlakile

options.sourceEnglish: Use it only on plants that are not eaten raw
options.sesothoDraft: A sebedise feela dimeleng tse sa jeweng di le tala

rationale.sourceEnglish: Guidance differs on some water sources and on the service conditions for reuse. A qualified local check is needed before deciding whether any source and use are suitable or allowed.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Ditaelo di fapana mabapi le mehlodi e meng ya metsi le maemo a ditshebeletso bakeng sa ho sebedisa metsi hape. Qualified local check e a hlokahala pele ho qeto ya hore na mohlodi ofe kapa ofe le tshebediso di loketse kapa di dumelletswe.

question.sourceEnglish: Why check the exact water source and cleaning products before considering reuse?
question.sesothoDraft: Hobaneng ho lokela ho hlahlojwa mohlodi o tobileng wa metsi le dihlahiswa tsa ho hlwekisa pele ho nahanwa ka ho a sebedisa hape?

options.sourceEnglish: All cleaning products are safe if the water is diluted
options.sesothoDraft: Dihlahiswa tsohle tsa ho hlwekisa di bolokehile haeba metsi a hlapolotswe

options.sourceEnglish: Water composition and product effects vary, so the actual source and products need assessment
options.sesothoDraft: Sebopeho sa metsi le ditlamorao tsa dihlahiswa di a fapana, kahoo mohlodi wa sebele le dihlahiswa di hloka tlhahlobo

options.sourceEnglish: The water can be reused when it has no smell
options.sesothoDraft: Metsi a ka sebediswa hape ha a se na monko

options.sourceEnglish: Mulch removes every harmful substance
options.sesothoDraft: Mulch e tlosa ntho e nngwe le e nngwe e kotsi

rationale.sourceEnglish: Used water can contain different germs, salts and chemicals. Neither clear appearance, lack of smell nor mulch proves that it is safe or suitable.
rationale.sesothoDraft: Metsi a sebedisitsweng a ka ba le dikokwana-hloko, matswai le dikhemikhale tse fapaneng. Ho shebahala a hlakile ha ho pake hore a bolokehile kapa a loketse; ho hloka monko ha ho pake seo, le mulch ha e pake seo.

title.sourceEnglish: Water Harvesting

description.sourceEnglish: Swales, berms, dams, rainwater tanks and greywater — slow, spread and sink every drop.
description.tshivendaDraft: Swales, berms, dams, rainwater tanks na greywater — fhungudzani luvhilo, phaḓaladzani nahone sink every drop.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Concept cross-section of a level contour swale with a raised mound below it. Arrows show runoff slowing and spreading; infiltration depends on the soil and site.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Concept cross-section ya level contour swale i re na mound yo takuwaho fhasi hayo. Misevhe i sumbedza runoff i tshi fhungudza luvhilo na u phaḓalala; infiltration i ḓitika nga mavu na fhethu.

title.sourceEnglish: Swales and Berms: Slowing Water on the Slope
title.tshivendaDraft: Swales na Berms: U Fhungudza Luvhilo lwa Maḓi kha U Sendama ha Mavu

body.sourceEnglish:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Lushaka luthihi lwa swale ndi level trench on contour. I fhungudza luvhilo na u phaḓaladza runoff, uri maḓi maṅwe a kone u dzhena kha mavu o teaho. Dziṅwe swales dzi itelwa u vha na slight, controlled grade uri dzi hwale maḓi o engedzeaho nga u ongologa a tshi ya kha safe outlet. Nḓila ine ya fanelea your land i bva kha mavu, slope, drainage na storm flow. Musi ni sa athu u bwa, humbelani trained local adviser uri a sedze line, overflow na receiving point.

Mavu o bwiwaho a vhumba berm nga thungo ya downhill, hune miri ya nga ṱavhiwa arali site design yo tea.

Miri yo ṱavhiwaho henefho i nga shumisa moisture yo vhulungwaho mavuni nga murahu ha mvula, zwi tshi ya nga site.

Mvula khulwane i nga ḓadza swale nga luvhilo lu fhiraho lune maḓi a dzhena ngalwo mavuni. Pulani safe overflow ni sa athu u bwa.

Nḓila a i tei u erode slope kana u rumela maḓi a tshinyaho kha muhura. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Humbelani trained local adviser uri a ṱole mavu, slope na storm flow. Tshifanyiso a si construction design.

Slope fhedzi a i sumbedzi arali swale yo tea. Mavu, drainage, unstable ground na maḓi ane a bva upslope zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

Vhulungani ground cover yavhuḓi. Wanani local assessment ni sa athu u bwa kha steep, wet kana unstable land. Grass barriers na terraces na zwone zwi ṱoḓa design yo teaho site.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A level contour swale can hold runoff for infiltration on a suitable site; other swales need a designed grade and safe outlet
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Level contour swale i nga fara runoff uri hu vhe na infiltration kha site yo teaho; dziṅwe swales dzi ṱoḓa designed grade na safe outlet

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep good ground cover and plan a safe overflow
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Vhulungani ground cover yavhuḓi nahone ni pulane safe overflow

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Assess soil, drainage, slope and storm flow before digging
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani mavu, drainage, slope na storm flow ni sa athu u bwa

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A concept picture is not a construction design
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Tshifanyiso tsha concept a si construction design

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer planned a level contour swale. After heavy rain, one end holds most of the water. What should the farmer check before changing the earthwork?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi o pulana level contour swale. Nga murahu ha mvula khulwane, magumo mathihi a fara vhunzhi ha maḓi. Mulimi u tea u ṱola mini a sa athu u shandula earthwork?

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the trench can be made deeper without a site check
options.tshivendaDraft: Arali trench i tshi nga itwa yo dzikaho u fhira hu si na site check

options.sourceEnglish: The intended design and measured levels with a trained local adviser; an unintended low point may be present
options.tshivendaDraft: Design yo pulaniwaho na measured levels zwi tshi ṱolwa na trained local adviser; unintended low point i nga vha hone

options.sourceEnglish: Whether a new dam at the lowest point will catch every overflow
options.tshivendaDraft: Arali dam ntswa kha lowest point i tshi ḓo fara overflow iṅwe na iṅwe

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the soil should be compacted to stop all infiltration
options.tshivendaDraft: Arali mavu a tshi tea u compacted uri hu imiswe infiltration yoṱhe

rationale.sourceEnglish: A level contour design should spread water along its length. Uneven filling may indicate an unintended low point, but some swales are intentionally graded to a safe outlet. Check the actual design, soil and overflow route before altering it.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Level contour design i tea u phaḓaladza maḓi kha vhulapfu hayo. U ḓala hu sa lingani hu nga sumbedza unintended low point, fhedzi dziṅwe swales dzi itwa nga khole dzi na grade ya u ya kha safe outlet. Ṱolani design ya vhukuma, mavu na overflow route ni sa athu u i shandula.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to control erosion on steep land. What should she do before digging?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi u ṱoḓa u langa erosion kha steep land. U tea u ita mini a sa athu u bwa?

options.sourceEnglish: Standard swales dug as deep as possible
options.tshivendaDraft: Standard swales dzo bwiwaho dza dzika nga hune zwa konadzea ngaho

options.sourceEnglish: Keep ground covered and get a site assessment for suitable erosion controls
options.tshivendaDraft: Itani uri mavu a dzule o funengetea nahone ni wane site assessment ya erosion controls dzo teaho

options.sourceEnglish: A large dam at the bottom to catch all runoff
options.tshivendaDraft: Dam khulwane fhasi uri i fare runoff yoṱhe

options.sourceEnglish: Compacting the soil surface with a roller
options.tshivendaDraft: U compact-a nṱha ha mavu nga roller

rationale.sourceEnglish: Slope alone is not enough to choose an earthwork. Soil, drainage, stability and storm flow must also be assessed.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Slope fhedzi a yo ngo lingana u khetha earthwork. Mavu, drainage, stability na storm flow na zwone zwi tea u ṱolwa.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: A farm dam cut through the middle: water flowing in at one end, the stored body of water, a spillway at the top edge for overflow, and a planted bank holding the soil.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Dam ya bulasini yo sumbedzwaho yo tsheiwa vhukati: maḓi a tshi elela a tshi dzhena kha magumo mathihi, maḓi o vhulungwaho, spillway kha muṅwenda wa nṱha ya overflow, na bank yo ṱavhiwaho zwimela ine ya fara mavu.

title.sourceEnglish: Farm Dams and Ponds: Storing Water for the Dry Season
title.tshivendaDraft: Madamu na Zwidziva zwa Bulasini: U Vhulunga Maḓi a Tshifhinga tsha Dry Season

body.sourceEnglish:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Dam kana pond i nga vhulunga runoff, fhedzi maḓi ane a wanala a bva kha mvula ya henefho, catchment, maḓi a xelaho na uri ni shumisa maḓi mangana.

Tshifhinga tsha mvula tshi a fhambana u mona na Afurika Tshipembe. Shumisani rekhodo dza henefho nahone ni pulanele zwifhinga zwo omaho; dam yo ḓalaho a yo khwaṱhisedzwi.

Musi ni sa athu u shandula watercourse kana u fhaṱa storage works, ṱolani authorisation ine ya ṱoḓea kha water authority.

Dam i ṱoḓa site investigation na design yo itwaho nga suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, mavu, foundations, downstream risk na safe spillway zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

Ni songo humbula uri mvula ya ṅwaha woṱhe i ni vhudza vhuhulwane ha flood kana storage ine na ḓo vha nayo.

Overflow i songo langiwaho i nga erode na breach wall. Pulani nḓila yo tsireledzeaho ya maḓi o engedzeaho ni sa athu u thoma construction.

Maḓi a nga xela nga evaporation na seepage. Sedzani water level, ni ṱole leaks kana erosion.

Itani uri spillway i dzule i si na zwine zwa i thivhela nahone ni ṱhogomele bank cover yo bulwaho kha design. Ni songo ṱavha miri kha earth dam wall.

Zwipuka zwi nga tshinya banks nahone zwa engedza manure kha maḓi. U vha hone hadzo a hu iti uri maḓi a vhe o kunaho kana o tsireledzeaho.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A dam needs a site assessment and qualified design
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Dam i ṱoḓa site assessment na design yo itwaho nga qualified person.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Design a safe spillway before construction
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Itani design ya safe spillway ni sa athu u thoma construction

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Check required water authorisations before building
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani authorisations a ṱoḓeaho a maḓi ni sa athu fhaṱa.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Maintain bank cover and keep trees off an earth dam wall
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱhogomelani bank cover nahone ni ite uri miri i si vhe kha earth dam wall

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer builds a dam wall with no spillway. After an exceptional storm it overflows. What's the likely result?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi u fhaṱa dam wall i si na spillway. Nga murahu ha exceptional storm, dam i a overflow. Ndi mvelelo ifhio ine ya nga tevhela?

options.sourceEnglish: The water irrigates lower fields beneficially
options.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi a sheledza masimu a re fhasi nga ndila ya vhuyedzo.

options.sourceEnglish: It overtops and erodes the wall, risking a catastrophic breach
options.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi a fhira nga nṱha ha wall na u erode wall, zwa ita uri hu vhe na khombo ya catastrophic breach.

options.sourceEnglish: The dam stays full and overflow drains harmlessly
options.tshivendaDraft: Dam i dzula yo ḓala nahone overflow i bva nga ndila i si na khombo.

options.sourceEnglish: Storage capacity increases permanently
options.tshivendaDraft: Storage capacity i engedzea tshifhinga tshoṱhe.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Without a designed overflow route, excess water finds its own way over the wall — and that uncontrolled flow is what erodes and eventually breaches it.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Hu si na overflow route yo itwaho nga design, maḓi o engedzeaho a wana ndila yao ya u fhira nga nṱha ha wall — nahone ndi u elela honoho hu songo langiwaho hune ha erode wall na u fhedza hu tshi i breach.

question.sourceEnglish: Which action helps protect an earth dam?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi vhukando vhufhio vhune ha thusa u tsireledza earth dam?

options.sourceEnglish: A deep, exposed dam with no bank vegetation
options.tshivendaDraft: Dam yo dzikaho, exposed, i si na zwimela kha bank

options.sourceEnglish: Maintain the designed bank cover and keep the spillway clear
options.tshivendaDraft: Ṱhogomelani bank cover yo bulwaho kha design nahone ni ite uri spillway i dzule i si na zwine zwa i thivhela

options.sourceEnglish: A full concrete lining and plastic cover
options.tshivendaDraft: Concrete lining yo fhelelaho na plastic cover.

options.sourceEnglish: A larger surface area to spread evaporation evenly
options.tshivendaDraft: Surface area khulwane u phaḓaladza evaporation nga ndinganelo.

rationale.sourceEnglish: A clear spillway and maintained banks help the dam work as designed. Trees should not be planted on an earth dam wall.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Spillway i si na zwine zwa i thivhela na banks dzi ṱhogomelwaho zwi thusa dam uri i shume nga nḓila yo bulwaho kha design. Miri a i tei u ṱavhiwa kha earth dam wall.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Rain running off a roof into a gutter and down a pipe into a tank, with a small first-flush diverter branching off before the tank to throw away the dirty first water.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi a mvula a tshi elela a tshi bva kha ṱhanga a dzhena kha gutter nahone a tsa nga pipe a dzhena kha tank, hu na first-flush diverter ṱhukhu i bva kha pipe musi i sa athu u swika kha tank uri i bvise maḓi a u thoma a re na tshika.

title.sourceEnglish: Rainwater Tanks and Roof Catchment: Collecting and Protecting Water
title.tshivendaDraft: Rainwater Tanks na Roof Catchment: U kuvhanganya na u tsireledza maḓi

body.sourceEnglish:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Ṱhanga ya ṋu i nga kuvhanganya madi a mvula. Madi ane a wanala a bva kha vhuhulwane ha ṱhanga, mvula na madi a xelaho.

Ṱolani arali roof material yo tea u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula musi ni sa athu u ṱumanya tank.

Shumisani vhuhulwane ha ṱhanga vhune ha vhonala u bva nṱha na rekhodo dza mvula dza henefho. Nga murahu ni dzhiele nṱha maḓi ane a si dzhene kha gutter, ane a diverted kana ane a overflow kha tank yo ḓalaho.

Tshivhalo tsha ṅwaha woṱhe a tshi ni vhudzi uri hu ḓo vha na maḓi mangana kha dry spell. Vhambedzani supply na mishumo ine na pulana u shumisa maḓi hayo.

Runoff ya ṱhanga i nga hwala buse, droppings na iṅwe contamination. First-flush diverter i thivhela maṅwe maḓi a runoff ya u thoma uri a si dzhene kha tank.

Diversion ine ya ṱoḓea i ḓitika nga ṱhanga na system. Shumisani ndaela dza supplier dza sizing na maintenance; a hu na volume nthihi ine ya shuma kha ṱhanga iṅwe na iṅwe.

Diverter a i iti uri maḓi o salaho a vhe o tsireledzea u nwiwa.

Vhuhulwane ha tank vhu bva kha water demand, mvula, vhuhulwane ha ṱhanga na vhulapfu ha dry periods.

Ṅwalani mishumo yo pulaniwaho nahone ni anganyele demand yayo ni tshi shumisa rekhodo dzaṋu. Vhambedzani demand yayo na supply u mona na zwifhinga zwa ṅwaha.

Pulannani zwine na ḓo ita musi stored water runs low. Dzina ḽa vundu fhedzi a ḽi ni vhudzi vhuhulwane ha tank ine na i ṱoḓa.

Itani uri tank i dzule covered; vheani screen kha openings uri zwikhokhonono zwi si dzhene, nahone ni ṱhogomele ṱhanga, gutters na diverter. Vhulungani maḓi a mvula o fhambanywa na pipes dza maḓi a u nwa.

Maḓi ane a vhonala o kuna a nga kha ḓi vha na germs kana chemicals. Vhudzisani local health authority nga testing na treatment zwo teaho mushumo wo pulaniwaho.

Basic filter fhedzi a si drinking-water guarantee. Maḓi ane a shumiswa kha food crops na one a ṱoḓa safety assessment.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rain, demand and losses determine useful storage
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Vhuhulwane ha ṱhanga, mvula, water demand na maḓi a xelaho zwi laula maḓi ane a nga vhulungwa uri a shumisee.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Size and maintain the first-flush diverter for the roof
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Khethani sizing ya first-flush diverter yo teaho ṱhanga nahone ni i ṱhogomele

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Clear water can still contain germs or chemicals
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi ane a vhonala o kuna a nga kha ḓi vha na germs kana chemicals.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Testing and treatment must match the intended use
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Testing na treatment zwi tea u tea mushumo wo pulaniwaho

question.sourceEnglish: What information is needed to choose a rainwater tank?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi mafhungo afhio ane a ṱoḓea u khetha rainwater tank?

options.sourceEnglish: Only the province where the farm is located
options.tshivendaDraft: Vundu ḽine bulasi ya vha khaḽo fhedzi.

options.sourceEnglish: Roof area, rainfall pattern, water demand and collection losses
options.tshivendaDraft: Vhuhulwane ha ṱhanga, pattern ya mvula, water demand na maḓi a xelaho musi a tshi kuvhanganywa.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the amount of rain in one storm
options.tshivendaDraft: Tshivhalo tsha mvula ya storm nthihi fhedzi.

options.sourceEnglish: Only the price of the biggest available tank
options.tshivendaDraft: Mutengo wa tank khulwanesa ine ya wanala fhedzi.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Tank planning must compare usable supply with demand through wet and dry periods. One fixed regional size cannot do that.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: U pulana tank hu tea u vhambedza supply ine ya nga shumiswa na demand kha wet and dry periods. Sayizi nthihi ya region yo tiwaho a i nga koni u ita zwenezwo.

question.sourceEnglish: Why does a first-flush diverter matter even for irrigation-only tank water?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi ngani first-flush diverter i tshi vha na ndeme na musi maḓi a tank a tshi shumiswa kha u sheledza fhedzi?

options.sourceEnglish: It doesn't matter for irrigation, only drinking water
options.tshivendaDraft: A i na ndeme kha u sheledza, i na ndeme kha maḓi a u nwa fhedzi.

options.sourceEnglish: The first flush carries concentrated droppings, dust and pathogens that can contaminate edible crops
options.tshivendaDraft: First flush i hwala concentrated droppings, buse na pathogens dzine dza nga contaminate zwimela zwine zwa ḽiwa.

options.sourceEnglish: It's more acidic and changes soil pH over time
options.tshivendaDraft: I na acidity nnzhi u fhira nahone i shandula soil pH nga tshifhinga.

options.sourceEnglish: It stops the tank overfilling in storms
options.tshivendaDraft: I thivhela tank uri i sa ḓadzehe nga maḓi manzhi nga storms.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Diverting early runoff can reduce contamination, but it does not guarantee that later water is safe. Assess quality for the intended use.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: U divert-a runoff ya u thoma zwi nga fhungudza contamination, fhedzi a zwi khwaṱhisedzi uri maḓi a tevhelaho a tsireledzea. Ṱolani quality u ya nga mushumo wo pulaniwaho.

title.sourceEnglish: Greywater: Check Before Reuse
title.tshivendaDraft: Greywater: Ṱolani ni sa athu u shumisa hafhu

body.sourceEnglish:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Maḓi o shumiswaho hayani a nga vha na germs, salts, zwibveledzwa zwa u kunakisa na zwiṅwe zwithu. Tsivhudzo a i ṱalusi tshiko tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe nga nḓila nthihi. Tsivhudzo ya Afurika Tshipembe i fhambana nga ha maḓi a khishini na maḓi a u ṱanzwa zwiambaro.

Ni songo katela maḓi a toilet, maḓi a bvaho kha nappies, maḓi a u ṱanzwa muthu a lwalaho kana a u ṱanzwa zwipuka kha pulane ya u shumisa maḓi hafhu. Ni songo dovha na shumisa maḓi a re na chemicals dzi vhaisaho.

Ni sa athu u shumisa maḓi hafhu na luthihi, humbelani masipala na qualified local sanitation adviser uri vha ṱole exact source, tshumelo dza maḓi na sanitation dza muṱa, mushumo wo pulaniwaho na fhethu. Arali nyeletshedzo iyi i siho kana i sa pfali, ni songo shumisa maḓi hafhu.

Tshifanyiso tshi angaredzaho a si farm design. Mavu na mulch a zwi disinfect wastewater. Vheani wastewater kule na drinking-water plumbing nahone ni thivhele uri i kwame vhathu kana zwipuka. Ni songo i fafadzela, ni songo i tendela i tshi pool, nahone ni songo i tendela i tshi elela i tshi bva kha property i tshi ya tshiṱaraṱani, kha drain kana watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, litshani u a shumisa ni humbele qualified local advice.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Water sources and greywater guidance can differ
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Tshiko tsha maḓi na tsivhudzo ya greywater zwi nga fhambana.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Check the source, service status, intended use and site locally before any reuse
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Ṱolani tshiko, service status, mushumo wo pulaniwaho na fhethu locally ni sa athu u shumisa maḓi hafhu na luthihi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Mavu na mulch a zwi disinfect wastewater

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Prevent contact, spray, pooling, runoff and drinking-water cross-connections
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Thivhelani contact, spray, pooling, runoff na drinking-water cross-connections

question.sourceEnglish: What should happen before any household washwater is reused?
question.tshivendaDraft: Hu fanela u itea mini ni sa athu u shumisa hafhu maḓi afhio na afhio a u ṱanzwa a muṱa?

options.sourceEnglish: Direct it below mulch around a tree
options.tshivendaDraft: Livhisani maḓi fhasi ha mulch u mona na muri.

options.sourceEnglish: Ask the municipality and a qualified sanitation adviser to check the source, service status, intended use and site
options.tshivendaDraft: Humbelani masipala na qualified sanitation adviser uri vha ṱole tshiko, service status, mushumo wo pulaniwaho na fhethu

options.sourceEnglish: Use it if it looks clear
options.tshivendaDraft: A shumiseni arali a tshi vhonala o kuna

options.sourceEnglish: Use it only on plants that are not eaten raw
options.tshivendaDraft: I shumiseni kha zwimela fhedzi zwine zwi sa ḽiwe zwi songo bikiwa.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Guidance differs on some water sources and on the service conditions for reuse. A qualified local check is needed before deciding whether any source and use are suitable or allowed.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Tsivhudzo i a fhambana nga ha zwiṅwe zwiko zwa maḓi na service conditions dza u shumisa maḓi hafhu. Qualified local check i a ṱoḓea ni sa athu u dzhia tsheo ya uri tshiko tshifhio na tshifhio na mushumo ufhio na ufhio zwine zwa humbulwa zwo tea kana zwo tendelwa.

question.sourceEnglish: Why check the exact water source and cleaning products before considering reuse?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi ngani ri tshi fanela u ṱola exact water source na zwibveledzwa zwa u kunakisa ri sa athu humbula nga ha u shumisa maḓi hafhu?

options.sourceEnglish: All cleaning products are safe if the water is diluted
options.tshivendaDraft: Zwibveledzwa zwoṱhe zwa u kunakisa zwo tsireledzea arali maḓi o vanganywa na maṅwe.

options.sourceEnglish: Water composition and product effects vary, so the actual source and products need assessment
options.tshivendaDraft: Water composition na mvelelo dza zwibveledzwa zwi a fhambana; ngauralo tshiko tsha vhukuma na zwibveledzwa zwi ṱoḓa assessment.

options.sourceEnglish: The water can be reused when it has no smell
options.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi a nga shumiswa hafhu arali a si na munukho.

options.sourceEnglish: Mulch removes every harmful substance
options.tshivendaDraft: Mulch i bvisa zwithu zwoṱhe zwi vhaisaho.

rationale.sourceEnglish: Used water can contain different germs, salts and chemicals. Neither clear appearance, lack of smell nor mulch proves that it is safe or suitable.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Maḓi o shumiswaho a nga vha na germs, salts na chemicals zwo fhambanaho. U vhonala o kuna a zwi sumbedzi uri maḓi o tsireledzea kana o tea; u sa vha na munukho a zwi sumbedzi zwenezwo; na mulch a i sumbedzi zwenezwo.

title.sourceEnglish: Water Harvesting

description.sourceEnglish: Swales, berms, dams, rainwater tanks and greywater — slow, spread and sink every drop.
description.xitsongaDraft: Swales, berms, madamu, mathanki ya mati ya mpfula ni greywater — nonokisa, hangalasa — sink every drop.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Concept cross-section of a level contour swale with a raised mound below it. Arrows show runoff slowing and spreading; infiltration depends on the soil and site.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Xifaniso xa miehleketo xa xisele (swale) lexi ringaneke eka khanthura, xi tsemakanyiwile exikarhi, xi ri na khurhana ra misava (berm) ehansi ka xona. Miseve yi komba mati lama khulukaka ma nonoka naswona ma hangalaka; ku nghena ka mati emisaveni swi titshege hi misava na ndhawu.

title.sourceEnglish: Swales and Berms: Slowing Water on the Slope
title.xitsongaDraft: Swisele (swales) na Makhurhana ya Misava (berms): Ku Nonokisa Mati eNdhawini yo Rhelela

body.sourceEnglish:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Muxaka wun'we wa xisele (swale) i a level trench on contour. Wu nonokisa mati lama khulukaka (runoff) wu tlhela wu ma hangalasa, leswaku mati man’wana ma kota ku nghena eka misava leyi faneleke. Swisele swin'wana swi dizayiniwa hi a slight, controlled grade, leswaku swi rhwala excess water hi ku nonoka ku ya eka outlet leyi hlayisekeke. Ndlela leyi faneleke ndhawu ya wena yi titshege hi misava, ku rhelela, ku humesa mati na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela line, overflow na ndhawu leyi mati ma amukeriwaka eka yona u nga si cela.

Misava leyi celiweke yi endla khurhana ra misava (berm) etlhelweni ra le hansi, laha mirhi yi nga byariwaka kona loko dizayini ya ndhawu yi fanerile.

Mirhi leyi byariweke kona yi nga tirhisa ku tsakama loku hlayisiweke emisaveni endzhaku ka mpfula, swi ya hi ndhawu.

Mpfula ya matimba yi nga tata xisele hi ku hatlisa ku tlula hilaha mati ma nghenaka hakona emisaveni. Kunguhatela ndlela leyi hlayisekeke ya mati lama taleke u nga si cela.

Ndlela ya kona a yi fanelanga ku kukula misava ya ndhawu yo rhelela kumbe ku rhumela mati lama onhaka eka muakelani. Xisele (swale) kumbe damu leswi nga downstream swi fanele ku kota ku ma amukela hi ndlela leyi hlayisekeke.

Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela misava, ku rhelela na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Xifaniso a hi dizayini yo aka ha yona.

Ku rhelela ntsena a ku ku byeli loko xisele xi fanerile. Misava, ku humesa mati, misava leyi nga tiyangiki na mati lama taka hi le henhla ka ndhawu yo rhelela hinkwaswo swa nkoka.

Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile kahle. Kuma nkambelo wa laha kaya u nga si cela eka ndhawu leyi rhelelaka ngopfu, leyi nga tsakama kumbe leyi nga tiyangiki. Mindzilakano ya byanyi (grass barriers) na titerasi (terraces) na swona swi lava dizayini leyi faneleke ndhawu.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A level contour swale can hold runoff for infiltration on a suitable site; other swales need a designed grade and safe outlet
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Xisele lexi ringaneke eka khanthura xi nga khoma mati lama khulukaka leswaku ma nghena emisaveni eka ndhawu leyi faneleke; swisele swin'wana swi lava ku rhelela loku dizayiniweke na ndlela leyi hlayisekeke yo humesa mati

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Keep good ground cover and plan a safe overflow
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile kahle naswona u pulana laha mati yo tala ma nga khulukelaka kona hi vuhlayiseki.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Assess soil, drainage, slope and storm flow before digging
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Kambela misava, ku humesa mati, ku rhelela na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze u nga si cela

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A concept picture is not a construction design
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Xifaniso xa miehleketo a hi pulani yo aka ha yona.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer planned a level contour swale. After heavy rain, one end holds most of the water. What should the farmer check before changing the earthwork?
question.xitsongaDraft: Murimi u pulanile level contour swale. Endzhaku ka mpfula ya ntamu, makumu man’we ma khoma vunyingi bya mati. Xana murimi u fanele ku kambela yini a nga si cinca earthwork?

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the trench can be made deeper without a site check
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku vona loko xisele xi nga entisiwa ku nga ri na nkambelo wa ndhawu

options.sourceEnglish: The intended design and measured levels with a trained local adviser; an unintended low point may be present
options.xitsongaDraft: Dizayini leyi kunguhatiweke ni levels leti pimiweke swin’we ni mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke; low point leyi nga kunguhatiwangiki yi nga va kona

options.sourceEnglish: Whether a new dam at the lowest point will catch every overflow
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku vona loko damu lerintshwa eka ndhawu leyi nga ehansi ku hundza hinkwato ri ta khoma overflow yin’wana ni yin’wana

options.sourceEnglish: Whether the soil should be compacted to stop all infiltration
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku vona loko misava yi fanele ku endliwa compaction leswaku yi yimisa infiltration hinkwato

rationale.sourceEnglish: A level contour design should spread water along its length. Uneven filling may indicate an unintended low point, but some swales are intentionally graded to a safe outlet. Check the actual design, soil and overflow route before altering it.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Dizayini ya level contour yi fanele ku hangalasa mati eka vulehi bya yona. Ku tala loku nga ringaniki ku nga komba low point leyi nga kunguhatiwangiki, kambe swisele swin’wana swi endliwa grade hi xikongomelo leswaku mati ma ya eka outlet leyi hlayisekeke. Kambela dizayini ya xiviri, misava ni overflow route u nga si yi cinca.

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to control erosion on steep land. What should she do before digging?
question.xitsongaDraft: Murimi u lava ku lawula ku kukuleka ka misava eka ndhawu leyi rhelelaka ngopfu. Xana u fanele ku endla yini a nga si cela?

options.sourceEnglish: Standard swales dug as deep as possible
options.xitsongaDraft: Standard swales leswi ceriweke swi enta hi laha swi kotekaka hakona

options.sourceEnglish: Keep ground covered and get a site assessment for suitable erosion controls
options.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile naswona u kuma nkambelo wa ndhawu lowu kongomaneke ni tindlela leti faneleke to lawula ku kukuleka ka misava

options.sourceEnglish: A large dam at the bottom to catch all runoff
options.xitsongaDraft: Damu lerikulu endhawini ya le hansi leswaku ri khoma runoff hinkwato

options.sourceEnglish: Compacting the soil surface with a roller
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku endla compaction eka vuandlalo bya misava hi roller

rationale.sourceEnglish: Slope alone is not enough to choose an earthwork. Soil, drainage, stability and storm flow must also be assessed.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Ku rhelela ntsena a ku enelanga ku hlawula earthwork. Misava, drainage, stability ni ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze na swona swi fanele ku kamberiwa.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: A farm dam cut through the middle: water flowing in at one end, the stored body of water, a spillway at the top edge for overflow, and a planted bank holding the soil.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Damu ra purasi, ri tsemakanyiwile hi le xikarhini: mati ma nghena eka makumu man’we, mati lama hlayisiweke, spillway emakumu ya le henhla ya overflow, ni bank leyi byariweke leyi khomaka misava.

title.sourceEnglish: Farm Dams and Ponds: Storing Water for the Dry Season
title.xitsongaDraft: Madamu ya Mapurasi na Swidziva: Ku Hlayisa Mati eka Nguva yo Oma

body.sourceEnglish:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Damu kumbe xidziva xi nga hlayisa mati lama khulukaka ehenhla ka misava, kambe ntsengo lowu kumekaka wu titshege hi mpfula ya le kusuhi, ndhawu yo hlengeleta mati (catchment), ku lahleka ka mati na leswaku u tirhisa mati yo tala njhani.

Tinguva ta mpfula ti hambana eAfrika Dzonga hinkwaro. Tirhisa tirhekhodo ta le kusuhi naswona u kunguhatela minkarhi yo oma; damu leri teleke a ri tiyisisiwi.

U nga si cinca watercourse kumbe ku aka storage works, kambela authorisation leyi lavekaka eka water authority.

Damu ri lava site investigation na design hi munhu loyi a nga na qualifications leti faneleke. Catchment runoff, misava, foundations, downstream risk ni spillway leyi hlayisekeke, hinkwato i swa nkoka.

U nga ehleketi leswaku ntsengo wa mpfula ya lembe wu ku byela vukulu bya ndhambi kumbe vuhlayiselo lebyi u nga ta va na byona.

Overflow leyi nga lawuriwiki yi nga erode and breach khumbi. Kunguhatela ndlela leyi hlayisekeke ya mati lama taleke u nga si sungula ku aka.

Mati ma nga lahleka hi evaporation na seepage. Kamba mpimo wa mati naswona lavisisa ku huma ka mati kumbe ku kukuleka ka misava.

Hlayisa spillway yi nga pfaleki naswona hlayisa bank cover leyi boxiweke eka design. U nga byali mirhi ehenhla ka earth dam wall.

Swiharhi swi nga onha banks na ku engetela vulongo ematini. Ku va kona ka swona a swi endli mati ma basa kumbe ma hlayiseka.
